term: well-founded global union of necessary existential-support edges
definition: The cross-world union of direct existential-support relations restricted to de re necessary individuals is well-founded. In finite models this rules out directed cycles (including nontrivial SCCs); in infinite models acyclicity alone does not establish well-foundedness. This permits world-varying edges that do not create a global regress.
note: Alternative open condition to direct edge invariance, weaker than full necessary-edge inclusion with actual well-foundedness, and not an assertion that actual metaphysical dependence has an ordinal rank. This is an optional cross-world overlay constraint, strictly stronger than worldwise well-foundedness of the same necessary-support-restricted relations. It does not imply well-foundedness of the full world-local causal relations and is not a default causal-coherence law or a consequence of temporal logic. Edges themselves never cross worlds.
